The effect was strongest for long and difficult texts.

lines.text: “My dear Mr. Bennet,”
lines.speaker: Mrs. Bennet

lines.text: said his lady to him one day,
“have you heard that Netherfield Park is let at last?”
lines.speaker: Mrs. Bennet

lines.text: Mr. Bennet replied that he had not.
“But it is,”
lines.speaker: Mrs. Bennet

lines.text: returned she;
“for Mrs. Long has just been here, and she told me all about it.”
lines.speaker: Mrs. Bennet

lines.text: Mr. Bennet made no answer.
“Do you not want to know who has taken it?”
lines.speaker: Mrs. Bennet

lines.text: cried his wife impatiently.
“You want to tell me, and I have no objection to hearing it.”
lines.speaker: Mr. Bennet

text: “You promised me you would be there,” said Maya.
“I said I would try,” Ravi said. “That is not the same thing, and you know—”
“It is exactly the same thing!” Maya shouted.
“Both of you, stop it,” said Grandmother quietly. “Sit down, both of you.”

meanings.text: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife.

truth.definition: a fact that has been verified

acknowledged.definition: recognized or made known or admitted

possession.definition: the act of having and controlling property

fortune.definition: a large amount of wealth or prosperity

want.definition: the state of needing something that is absent or unavailable
